name: SoraDigital SEO Optimizer
author: soradigital

sections.description:
SoraDigital SEO Optimizer is a full-featured SEO plugin built around one simple idea: every feature is free. There is no pro tier, no feature lock, no account to create and no registration nag. The things comparable plugins reserve for paid plans — advanced schema types, a redirect manager, indexing tools, Search Console data inside wp-admin — are all included and fully working.

Schema without the paywall

  • 18 schema types for the main content type, including Course, Book, Job Posting and Software Application, each labelled with its current rich-result status (active, conditional, or semantic only) so you know what Google actually does with it.
  • A guided builder adds up to 5 extra schema nodes per post (15 form-based types) — no JSON writing required. A raw custom JSON-LD field remains available for anything else.
  • Global schema templates: set a default schema type per post type; it applies automatically — with the same automatic fields as a manual choice — whenever a post has no schema type of its own. A per-post choice always wins.
  • FAQ, HowTo and Recipe are written once, inside the post content (Gutenberg block recommended; the text shortcode pattern is also supported): the visible section and the schema come from the same single source, so they can never drift apart.
  • HowTo detection: if a post has no HowTo shortcode or block, a HowTo is also detected from a plain steps section in the body — a heading that announces steps (for example “Langkah-langkah…”, “Cara…”, “How to…” or “Tutorial…”) followed by an ordered list or a run of sub-headings with at least 3 steps. Detection only adds schema; the body itself is never modified, and an explicit shortcode or block always wins.

Redirects and 404s

  • Redirect manager with exact rules and prefix wildcards, a 404 monitor, automatic redirects when a published slug changes, and redirect suggestions generated from your real 404 log.

Indexing and Search Console

  • Google Indexing API with multiple Google Cloud projects: add several service account keys and the plugin rotates across them, multiplying your daily quota, with a persistent queue and per-URL log.
  • Built-in Search Console statistics — clicks, impressions, CTR and average position for the whole site and per post, including the top queries for each URL — using the same service account keys.
  • Per-URL index status from the URL Inspection API, shown in each post’s editor panel and in a site-wide list, with a one-click hand-off to the Indexing API when a URL is not indexed yet.
  • Keyword position history: weekly snapshots of your top keywords’ average positions (plus a manual snapshot button), with previous-position and change columns and a biggest-movers list — a position tracker built entirely on your own Search Console data, free.
  • IndexNow: optionally notify participating search engines (Bing, Yandex and others) automatically when a post is published or its slug changes. The API key is generated for you and its key file is served by the plugin itself — no physical file is created. Off by default; drafts and trashed posts are never sent; a manual “submit homepage & latest posts” button and a short submission log are included.

Everyday SEO

  • Meta titles/descriptions with template variables, per-term overrides, Open Graph and Twitter Cards, canonical and robots control.
  • XML sitemap with image sitemap, a video sitemap (YouTube, Vimeo and video files extracted from post content; listed in the sitemap index only when it has entries) and a Google News sitemap (posts from the last 48 hours; always listed in the index), per-post hreflang pairs, automatic table of contents (shortcode, editor buttons, Gutenberg block) that never duplicates a hardcoded TOC, keeps FAQ questions as a single TOC entry, and titles itself in the post’s language on multilingual sites.
  • On-page SEO score (11 checks) in the editor, plus content health scans that find orphaned posts, duplicate featured images, duplicate SEO titles and meta descriptions (comparing the effective title — SEO title with a WordPress title fallback — and showing which source each post uses), and images without alt text (body images with a missing or empty alt attribute plus featured images without alt, worst posts first, up to 20).
  • A bulk meta editor for fixing SEO titles, descriptions and focus keywords across many posts at once, and settings export/import as JSON — configuration only; keys and data never travel.
  • Webmaster verification for Google, Bing, Baidu, Yandex, Pinterest and Norton Safe Web (plus custom meta tags): paste the code or the full meta tag — the code is extracted automatically — and the tags are printed in the head while head output is active.
  • A Status & Tools page: a copyable system status report (plugin, WordPress, theme, plugins, server, database, constants, filesystem permissions) with a read-only error log viewer, plus database maintenance tools — clear the plugin cache/transients, clear the 404 log, re-create missing plugin tables, and recalculate all SEO scores in batches.

Switching is safe

The migration tool imports post meta and Open Graph data, redirects, and a subset of schema from your previous SEO plugin. It previews counts before it runs, never overwrites data SoraDigital SEO Optimizer already has, and never deletes the source data — so rolling back is simply reactivating the old plugin. If another SEO plugin is active, SoraDigital SEO Optimizer automatically disables its own head output to prevent duplicate tags.

External services

This plugin can connect to the external services below only when an administrator enables the relevant module and configures their own credentials in the plugin settings. Nothing is sent anywhere before that, and the plugin never contacts the author’s servers — there are none.

  • Google Indexing API (https://indexing.googleapis.com) — used by the Indexing API module to notify Google when URLs are published, updated or deleted. Data sent: the URL and the notification type (URL_UPDATED or URL_DELETED), sent when a post is published/updated/deleted or when an administrator runs the queue manually. Authentication uses OAuth2 with your own Google Cloud service account keys; the service account must be an owner of the site property in Google Search Console for Google to accept notifications. Terms of Service: https://developers.google.com/terms — Privacy Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy
  • Google Search Console API (https://searchconsole.googleapis.com) — used by the Search Console module with a read-only scope and your own service account keys. It retrieves clicks, impressions, CTR and average position statistics for the property you configure and displays them in wp-admin; no site content is sent. The module also calls the URL Inspection endpoint of the same API: when an administrator clicks a “Check index status” button (or the weekly keyword snapshot runs), the plugin sends the inspected post URL and the configured property identifier to Google and stores the returned index verdict in the post’s metadata. Terms of Service: https://developers.google.com/terms — Privacy Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy
  • IndexNow (https://api.indexnow.org) — used only when an administrator enables IndexNow in the plugin settings. When a post is published or its slug changes (or the administrator clicks the manual submit button), the plugin sends the site host, the site’s public IndexNow API key, the key file location and the list of affected public URLs to the IndexNow endpoint, which relays them to participating search engines. The API key is not a secret: it is published by the plugin itself at /{key}.txt on your own site, as the protocol requires. Protocol documentation: https://www.indexnow.org/documentation — Terms of Service and privacy information: https://www.indexnow.org/terms

Service account private keys are stored encrypted in your own WordPress database.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the soradigital-seo-optimizer folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install the zip via Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate SoraDigital SEO Optimizer.
  3. On a fresh install, a four-step setup wizard opens automatically: your site details and type, feature defaults matched to that type, a one-click import from a previous SEO plugin (when its data is detected), and a summary with the optional Search Console / Indexing API next steps. The wizard can be skipped at any point and re-run later from SoraDigital SEO Optimizer → Settings; on upgrades it never opens by itself and never changes existing settings.
  4. Open SoraDigital SEO Optimizer → Settings to set your organization details, title separator and templates.
  5. Coming from another SEO plugin? Run SoraDigital SEO Optimizer → Migration — preview first, then import.
  6. Optional: add service account JSON keys under SoraDigital SEO Optimizer → Indexing API, then choose the Search Console property and project under Settings → Search Console.
sections.faq:
Is everything really free?

Yes. There is no pro version and nothing is locked, greyed out or limited to push an upgrade. There is also no account, registration or tracking — the plugin works fully offline from the author’s side because the author has no servers involved.

Can I migrate from my current SEO plugin?

Yes. The migration tool imports post meta (SEO title, description, focus keyword, canonical, robots) and Open Graph fields from Rank Math, Yoast SEO and All in One SEO (including the aioseo_posts table), imports redirects from the previous plugin’s redirect table, and converts a subset of stored schema (FAQ and HowTo become content shortcodes; simple Article, BlogPosting, NewsArticle and Product data becomes the main schema type). Every section previews its counts first, never overwrites existing SoraDigital SEO Optimizer data, and leaves the source data untouched.

What do I need for the Indexing API module?

Your own Google Cloud project with the Indexing API enabled and a service account JSON key. Add the key in the plugin, then add the service account email as an owner of your property in Google Search Console. You can add keys from several different projects; the plugin rotates across them (each project has its own 200 notifications/day quota from Google) and queues whatever exceeds the quota.

How do the Search Console statistics work?

They reuse the same service account keys with a read-only scope. Set the property (URL-prefix or sc-domain format) and the project in the settings, and make sure the property grants that service account access. Google’s data is delayed by roughly three days, and the plugin caches results for 12 hours. If access is missing you will get a clear 403 explanation in the admin instead of a blank page.

Why are FAQ, HowTo and Recipe written in the content?

Because copying the same questions into a meta box as a second source is error-prone. In SoraDigital SEO Optimizer you write them once, inside the content. The recommended path is the Gutenberg block (FAQ, HowTo and Recipe blocks with repeatable fields); the plain-text shortcode pattern — [sora_faq] with Q:/A: lines — remains fully supported for the classic editor and for migrated content, and its parser tolerates the markup WordPress auto-formatting (wpautop) produces around the lines. Either way, the rendered section your visitors see and the JSON-LD schema Google sees are generated from that one source. A HowTo can also come from a plain steps section written as normal article text (see the detection note in the Description); no shortcode is required for that.

What are the honest limitations?

HowTo detection only reads one steps section anchored by a heading that announces steps; a list or sub-headings elsewhere in the article are never turned into schema. The SEO score is a basic 11-point on-page heuristic — there is no readability analysis. There is no third-party rank tracker; keyword positions and their weekly history come from your real Search Console data instead, which only exists for sites you own and reflects average positions over the selected range, not a live SERP scrape. The schema builder is a guided form, not a free-form drag-and-drop builder. Hreflang pairs are entered manually per post. The interface is in English and fully translatable (text domain soradigital-seo-optimizer); translations are managed through translate.wordpress.org, where other languages can be contributed. Strings inside the Gutenberg block editor scripts are not yet translatable.

Does the plugin phone home or track me?

No. The only external requests are to Google’s APIs — only after you add your own service account keys — and, if you explicitly enable IndexNow, to the IndexNow endpoint, as described in the External services section above.
sections.changelog:
2.15.3

  • New: manual table-of-contents lists are migrated automatically at render time — a “Daftar isi” / “Table of Contents” heading followed by a plain list is recognized, its items become clickable links to the matching headings, and the automatic TOC is no longer added on top, so articles show a single working TOC with no content edits needed.
  • Fix: the default TOC title is now localized at render time — sites storing the English default “Table of Contents” (or an empty title) show the translated title (e.g. “Daftar Isi” on Indonesian sites) with no settings change; custom titles are unchanged.
  • Fix: cleaner TOC list without bullet markers — the TOC no longer draws its own bullets and suppresses theme list markers, so items show as a clean link list separated by hairlines.
  • Change: the TOC now lists H2 headings only by default (depth default changed from H2 + H3 to H2 only); sites with an explicitly saved depth keep theirs.

2.15.2

  • Fix: tables of contents left in content by another SEO plugin keep working after switching — heading anchor IDs are now added at render time even when an existing TOC is detected, so its stored links no longer point to missing anchors (our own TOC is still not added on those posts).

2.15.1

  • Fix: meta box saving in the block editor — the Search Console panel no longer nests a form inside the editor form, which previously made the editor’s save request carry the panel’s action and nonce instead of the post save, so meta box fields were silently not saved.

2.15.0

  • New: Breadcrumb display — show the breadcrumb trail with the [sseo_breadcrumb] shortcode or the new Breadcrumb block. It reuses the same trail as the BreadcrumbList schema (site name → ancestors/categories → current post), stays hidden on the homepage, and the separator and home label are configurable in Settings → Titles & Templates (shortcode attributes and block settings can override them per instance).
  • New: robots.txt editor in Status & Tools → robots.txt — custom content replaces the virtual robots.txt, with a read-only preview of the current effective output and a warning when a physical robots.txt file in the site root makes the editor ineffective.
  • New: Minimum Role setting (Settings → General) — choose the lowest role (Administrator, Editor, or Author) that can open and save the plugin’s admin screens. Only administrators can change this option; per-post checks such as the meta box are unchanged.

2.14.0

  • New: Auto Alt Text generator — fills missing image alt text from the attachment title or file name. Run it in bulk from Content Health → Images Without Alt Text (with a preview), or enable “Auto-generate alt text on upload” in Settings → General to fill new uploads automatically. Existing alt text is never overwritten, and camera-style or hash-like file names are skipped.
  • Fix: schema migration batches now always move forward — posts that are already migrated no longer use up the per-run batch, so repeated runs reach the whole site instead of rescanning the first batch.

2.13.0

  • Fix: redirect migration now reads the old plugin’s real table columns (url_to / header_code) — previously every rule was skipped as “empty destination” and no redirects were imported.
  • Fix: meta migration batches now always move forward — posts that are already filled no longer use up the per-run batch, so repeated runs reach the whole site instead of rescanning the first batch.
  • Fix: the %currentyear% template variable (plus the %name% and %sitedesc% aliases) is now supported in titles and descriptions, so migrated templates no longer print it literally.
  • Fix: when “Discourage search engines” (blog_public) is off, the robots meta tag now says noindex/nofollow and only one robots tag is printed (the core tag is suppressed on pages where SoraDigital SEO Optimizer prints its own).
  • New: the setup wizard pre-fills organization name, logo and social profiles (sameAs) from the previous SEO plugin when those fields are still empty, marked “Imported from your previous SEO plugin — review and save.” Nothing is saved until you save the step.
  • New: Global Settings migration on the Migration page — maps the old plugin’s site-wide settings (organization identity, title separator, homepage/search/404 and per-post-type templates, noindex switches, disabled date/author archives, advanced robots directives, per-taxonomy and author archive titles/descriptions/robots/schema switches, Local SEO business type, opening hours and email) into SoraDigital SEO Optimizer. Only settings still at their default are filled; anything already customized is left untouched, and a preview count is shown before running.

2.12.1

  • Tweak: in the Bulk Meta Editor, the pagination now sits on the same row as the Save Changes button (button left, pagination right) instead of below it.

2.12.0

  • New: Local SEO settings tab — a business profile (business name with fallback to the Organization Name, business type, postal address, phone, email, opening hours, price range, geo coordinates, map URL). When a name and address are filled in, a LocalBusiness schema node is added to the site-wide @graph next to the Organization node. All new settings are included in settings export/import.
  • Tweak: the Settings page tabs are reorganized — the long General tab is split up: Homepage & Archives templates moved to Titles & Templates, and the noindex switches, disable-archive switches, advanced robots directives, per-taxonomy archive controls and author archive controls moved to a new Archives & Robots tab. No settings, field names or behaviour changed.

The seven new settings are included in settings export/import.

  • Tweak: the active tab accent on the Settings, Content Health and Migration pages now uses the Sora logo blue instead of green.

2.9.1

2.9.0

  • Improvement: the Settings page is now organized into vertical tabs (General, Titles & Templates, Schema, Table of Contents, Sitemap, Hreflang, Search Console, Redirect, IndexNow, Tools) instead of one long scrolling page. It is the same single settings form underneath — every field, the save behavior, and all stored data are unchanged. The active tab is kept in the URL hash, so saving returns to the same tab; without JavaScript all sections remain visible exactly as before.

2.8.1

  • Shortened the plugin header description shown on the Plugins screen. No behavior, settings, or data changes.

2.8.0

  • Renamed: the plugin is now called SoraDigital SEO Optimizer (previously Sora SEO), with the new slug and text domain soradigital-seo-optimizer. All settings, stored data, post meta, schema, shortcodes and blocks keep working unchanged; settings exports made with older versions can still be imported.
  • Hardening from the wordpress.org review: admin inline scripts are now enqueued with wp_register_script/wp_add_inline_script; raw custom JSON-LD is validated before it is stored (invalid JSON is no longer saved); JSON-LD output is encoded so a </script> sequence inside a value can never break out of the script tag; translated admin strings are escaped on output; deprecated openssl_pkey_free() calls removed; the redundant load_plugin_textdomain() call was removed (WordPress loads translations automatically); external services (IndexNow, Google Indexing API, Google Search Console API) are documented with terms and privacy links in the readme.

2.7.10

  • Fix: template variables from the previous SEO plugin (such as %seo_title% and %seo_description%) no longer leak into migrated schema as literal text. During migration they are expanded to the post’s real SEO title, description, title, or excerpt, and a value that still contains an unknown variable is dropped so the normal fallback applies. Schema rendering now also treats a stored value containing a template variable as empty, so posts migrated earlier render the post title and excerpt instead of the raw variable, and Content Health lists any saved schema fields that still contain template variables.

2.7.9

  • Improvement: the table of contents now ships with a slimmer default style: links at 15px, the title at 16px, sub-level links at 14px, and tighter item spacing (3px padding, 1.3 line height). Sites that previously needed custom CSS overrides for a compact table of contents get the same look out of the box. Markup and settings are unchanged.

2.7.8

  • Fix: Recipe blocks and shortcodes with an explicitly empty title now render without a heading, matching HowTo since 2.7.4. Previously an empty title fell back to the post title, duplicating the article heading above the recipe; a missing title still falls back to the post title as before. Schema and extraction are unchanged.

2.7.7

  • Fix: the setup wizard could not advance past any step on hosts without PHP output buffering (including WordPress Playground): each step’s form was processed inside the page render, after the admin header had already been printed, so the redirect to the next step failed with “headers already sent” and the wizard content area came back blank. Wizard form submissions are now handled on admin_init, before any output, so every step transition redirects correctly on any host. No settings or data are changed.

2.7.6

  • Fix: text written as escaped markup inside HowTo, FAQ and Recipe block attributes (for example a configuration token written as <NOSRV>) disappeared from the schema: the block extractor decoded HTML entities across the whole attribute JSON first, so the decoded text was later mistaken for a real tag and stripped. Block attributes are now read the same way WordPress core reads them, and attribute text is unescaped exactly once when the schema plain text is built — escaped tokens survive as literal text, real markup is still stripped, and ordinary entities still decode exactly as before.

2.7.5

  • Fix: steps detected from the post body lost words that were written as escaped markup in the text (for example a configuration token written as <NOSRV>): the detection turned step text into plain text twice, and the second pass mistook the decoded text for a real tag and removed it, leaving a broken sentence in the HowTo schema. Detected steps are now converted to plain text exactly once, so escaped tokens survive as literal text. Real markup is still stripped and ordinary entities still decoded, exactly as before.

2.7.4

  • Fix: an explicitly empty title on a HowTo block or shortcode was replaced by the post title and printed as a heading inside the content, duplicating the article title. An empty title is now honored (no heading is printed); blocks and shortcodes saved without a title attribute keep the previous post-title fallback.

2.7.3

  • Documentation: added the wordpress.org contributor, screenshot captions and directory screenshots. No code changes.

2.7.2

  • Fix: the setup wizard page could not be opened. It was registered under the Sora SEO menu and then removed from the menu again, which makes WordPress deny access to the page itself — every user, administrators included, got the core “Sorry, you are not allowed to access this page.” error, so neither the Settings button nor the one-time post-activation redirect could ever reach it. The wizard is now registered as a hidden page (no menu entry) instead, which stays openable by administrators. No settings or data are changed.

2.7.1

  • The Plugin URI now points to the plugin’s home page at https://sora.ai.in/soraseo/, and the wordpress.org submission assets (icon and banners) were prepared. No behaviour changes.

2.7.0

  • New: setup wizard. On a fresh install, activation leads into a four-step wizard — (1) site: organization name and logo plus a site type (blog, business, online store, publisher/news); (2) features: sitemap (core, image, video, news), table of contents, smart redirects, IndexNow and hreflang, pre-selected with sensible defaults for the chosen site type; (3) import: when data from a previous SEO plugin is detected, one click runs the existing meta, redirect and schema migration; (4) finish: a summary of the saved choices with optional links to the Search Console and Indexing API setup. The wizard can be skipped at any step (skipping changes nothing beyond the steps already saved) and re-run at any time via the “Run the Setup Wizard” button in Settings. Upgrades are never redirected and no existing setting is changed unless it is edited in the wizard itself.
  • New: sitemap toggles. The video and news sitemaps can now be switched off (Settings keys sitemap_video / sitemap_news, on by default and settable from the wizard); a switched-off sitemap is dropped from the sitemap index and serves an empty sitemap at its own URL. Sites without the keys keep the previous behaviour exactly.

2.6.0

  • Fix: the [sora_faq] text shortcode could still render nothing on real sites. The Q:/A: parser split its input into blocks on blank lines, so content in which WordPress auto-formatting (wpautop) wraps every Q and A line in its own <p> produced no pairs at all. The parser now works line by line — every Q: line starts a new pair — and produces identical pairs for the raw text form, the <br /> form, one <p> per pair, one <p> per line, and mixed forms with inline markup. The rendered section and the FAQPage schema now agree on every form.
  • New: HowTo detection from the post body. When a post has no HowTo shortcode or block, the plugin looks for one steps section anchored by a heading that announces steps (Indonesian “langkah”/”cara”/”tutorial”, English “step”/”steps”/”how to”) and reads its steps from the first ordered list in that section, or from its sub-headings and their paragraphs when there is no list. At least 3 steps are required. The detected HowTo is added to the schema graph (named after the post title) unless the post’s main schema type is Product or Recipe; an explicit shortcode/block always wins. Schema only — the body and the table of contents are never changed.

2.5.3

  • Code hygiene only: internal development comments were removed throughout the plugin and the remaining documentation comments were shortened to brief, neutral one-liners. No behaviour changes, no new features, no settings or data changes.

2.5.2

  • Fix: the automatic rewrite flush on version change (added in 2.5.1) only ran on admin_init, so a site updated by overwriting files or via WP-CLI — without anyone visiting wp-admin — kept its old rewrite rules and new routes (e.g. the news/video sitemaps) stayed 404 for front-end traffic. The upgrade check now also runs on init (after the plugin’s own rule registrars), so the first front-end request after an update re-registers the rules, flushes once, and records the new version; admin_init is kept as a backstop. No settings or data are changed.

2.5.1

  • Fix: FAQ sections written with the text shortcode pattern could disappear from the rendered page on real article content. WordPress auto-formatting (wpautop) turns the shortcode’s lines into <br /> followed by a newline; the parser normaliser converted the <br> to a newline without consuming the existing one, so every Q and A landed in a separate block and no pairs were recognised (the FAQPage schema, which reads the raw content, kept working, so nothing looked wrong). The normaliser now consumes at most one following newline, and <br> variants with attributes are handled too.
  • Fix: sites updated by overwriting the plugin files (without reactivation) never received rewrite rules added by newer versions — e.g. the video/news sitemaps and the IndexNow key file from 2.5.0 could 404 until permalinks were flushed manually. The version upgrade routine now re-registers all of the plugin’s rewrite rules and performs a soft flush whenever the stored version differs from the running one.

2.5.0

  • IndexNow: new module that notifies participating search engines (Bing, Yandex and others) when a post is published or its slug changes. The API key is generated automatically when IndexNow is first enabled (and can be regenerated), the key file is served by the plugin at /{key}.txt without a physical file, submissions are logged (time, URL count, HTTP status), and a manual “submit homepage & latest posts” button is included. Off by default.
  • Global schema templates: a default schema type per post type in Settings, applied with the same automatic fields as a manual choice whenever a post has no schema type of its own; a per-post choice always wins.
  • Content health: three new scans — duplicate SEO titles (effective title: SEO title meta with a WordPress title fallback, source shown per post), duplicate meta descriptions, and images without alt text (body images with missing/empty alt plus featured images without alt, worst 20 posts).
  • Video sitemap (sitemap-video.xml): YouTube (watch, youtu.be, embed, shorts), Vimeo and video files are extracted from post content; each entry carries a thumbnail (from the YouTube video ID, or the post thumbnail for other sources), the post title and the meta description. Listed in the sitemap index only when it has entries.
  • News sitemap (sitemap-news.xml): posts published in the last 48 hours (max 1,000) with publication name and language from the site; always listed in the sitemap index.

2.4.0

  • TOC guard: the automatic table of contents now detects a hardcoded TOC from another source in a post’s content and skips that post entirely, so a TOC can never appear twice; Sora SEO’s own shortcode/block markers are not treated as foreign TOCs. The Settings page warns when recent posts already contain hardcoded TOCs.
  • TOC: headings inside an FAQ section no longer become TOC sub-entries — the FAQ section itself stays as exactly one entry — and on Polylang sites the TOC title follows the post’s language (Indonesian “Daftar Isi” / English “Table of Contents”) instead of the stored setting.
  • Settings export/import: download the global configuration as JSON and import it on another site; only known setting keys are applied (sanitized, unknown keys reported). Service account keys and all stored data are never exported.
  • New Bulk Meta Editor submenu: edit SEO titles, meta descriptions and focus keywords for published posts and pages, 20 per page with title search and a post-type filter; only changed rows are saved and their SEO scores are recalculated immediately.

2.3.0

  • Search Console: per-URL index status via the URL Inspection API — status (indexed / not indexed / error) with coverage state and last crawl time in each post’s editor panel and in a site-wide Index Status list (single checks plus a “check first 20 unchecked” batch), cached per post for 24 hours; posts that are not indexed get a one-click “Submit via Indexing API” button.
  • Search Console: keyword position history — weekly snapshots (WP-Cron) plus a manual “Take snapshot now” button, storing up to 26 snapshots of the top 100 keywords; the Top Keywords table gains Previous and Change columns, and a history section lists the snapshots and the biggest risers and fallers between the last two.

2.2.0

  • Full internationalisation: every user-facing string now uses the sora-seo text domain with English as the source language; an official Indonesian (id_ID) translation ships in languages/, so Indonesian sites keep the exact same interface wording as before.

2.1.1

  • Public-release preparation: migration source keys and table names are now written as plain literals (identical values, previously assembled from string parts) so the code is easy to audit; added this wordpress.org readme. No functional changes.

2.1.0

  • Guided schema builder: up to 5 additional schema nodes per post from 15 form-based types, stored alongside the main schema type.

2.0.0

  • Search Console module: site-wide and per-post clicks, impressions, CTR and average position, plus top queries per URL, using your Indexing API service accounts (read-only, cached 12 hours).

1.9.2

  • Blog-home (posts page) uses its own meta and canonical; archive pages output a CollectionPage JSON-LD graph; sitemap queries are no longer filtered by Polylang’s default language.

1.9.1

  • Database fix: key columns are varchar(191) so table creation also succeeds on databases with a 1000-byte index limit; idempotent table installer and automatic DB version upgrade.

1.9.0

  • Migration expanded: redirect import, All in One SEO as a meta source, schema subset migration; rich-result status labels for every schema type.

1.8.0

  • Per-post hreflang pairs with x-default control; image sitemap.

1.7.0

  • HowTo and Recipe are now single-source from post content (shortcode/block), like FAQ.

1.6.1

  • FAQ meta box removed entirely; FAQ schema comes only from the post content.

1.6.0

  • FAQ is single-source from post content (shortcode/block renders the section and the FAQPage schema).

1.5.0

  • Smart redirects: prefix wildcards, automatic redirects on slug changes, redirect suggestions from the 404 log.

1.4.0

  • Head output for the homepage, archives, author pages, search and 404; option to disable the core WordPress sitemap in favour of the plugin sitemap.

1.3.0

  • Automatic table of contents with shortcode, editor buttons and a Gutenberg block.

1.2.0

  • Migration of post meta and Open Graph data from a previous SEO plugin.

1.1.0

  • SEO score panel in the editor (11 on-page checks) and a score column in post lists.

1.0.0

  • Initial release: meta and templates, Open Graph/Twitter Cards, XML sitemap, 18 schema types, redirect manager with 404 monitor, content health checks, multi-project Google Indexing API.

short_description: Complete SEO toolkit — meta, 18 schema types, smart redirects, multi-project Indexing API and Search Console stats. Every feature is free.
description:
SoraDigital SEO Optimizer is a full-featured SEO plugin built around one simple idea: every feature is free. There is no pro tier, no feature lock, no account to create and no registration nag. The things comparable plugins reserve for paid plans — advanced schema types, a redirect manager, indexing tools, Search Console data inside wp-admin — are all included and fully working.

Schema without the paywall

  • 18 schema types for the main content type, including Course, Book, Job Posting and Software Application, each labelled with its current rich-result status (active, conditional, or semantic only) so you know what Google actually does with it.
  • A guided builder adds up to 5 extra schema nodes per post (15 form-based types) — no JSON writing required. A raw custom JSON-LD field remains available for anything else.
  • Global schema templates: set a default schema type per post type; it applies automatically — with the same automatic fields as a manual choice — whenever a post has no schema type of its own. A per-post choice always wins.
  • FAQ, HowTo and Recipe are written once, inside the post content (Gutenberg block recommended; the text shortcode pattern is also supported): the visible section and the schema come from the same single source, so they can never drift apart.
  • HowTo detection: if a post has no HowTo shortcode or block, a HowTo is also detected from a plain steps section in the body — a heading that announces steps (for example “Langkah-langkah…”, “Cara…”, “How to…” or “Tutorial…”) followed by an ordered list or a run of sub-headings with at least 3 steps. Detection only adds schema; the body itself is never modified, and an explicit shortcode or block always wins.

Redirects and 404s

  • Redirect manager with exact rules and prefix wildcards, a 404 monitor, automatic redirects when a published slug changes, and redirect suggestions generated from your real 404 log.

Indexing and Search Console

  • Google Indexing API with multiple Google Cloud projects: add several service account keys and the plugin rotates across them, multiplying your daily quota, with a persistent queue and per-URL log.
  • Built-in Search Console statistics — clicks, impressions, CTR and average position for the whole site and per post, including the top queries for each URL — using the same service account keys.
  • Per-URL index status from the URL Inspection API, shown in each post’s editor panel and in a site-wide list, with a one-click hand-off to the Indexing API when a URL is not indexed yet.
  • Keyword position history: weekly snapshots of your top keywords’ average positions (plus a manual snapshot button), with previous-position and change columns and a biggest-movers list — a position tracker built entirely on your own Search Console data, free.
  • IndexNow: optionally notify participating search engines (Bing, Yandex and others) automatically when a post is published or its slug changes. The API key is generated for you and its key file is served by the plugin itself — no physical file is created. Off by default; drafts and trashed posts are never sent; a manual “submit homepage & latest posts” button and a short submission log are included.

Everyday SEO

  • Meta titles/descriptions with template variables, per-term overrides, Open Graph and Twitter Cards, canonical and robots control.
  • XML sitemap with image sitemap, a video sitemap (YouTube, Vimeo and video files extracted from post content; listed in the sitemap index only when it has entries) and a Google News sitemap (posts from the last 48 hours; always listed in the index), per-post hreflang pairs, automatic table of contents (shortcode, editor buttons, Gutenberg block) that never duplicates a hardcoded TOC, keeps FAQ questions as a single TOC entry, and titles itself in the post’s language on multilingual sites.
  • On-page SEO score (11 checks) in the editor, plus content health scans that find orphaned posts, duplicate featured images, duplicate SEO titles and meta descriptions (comparing the effective title — SEO title with a WordPress title fallback — and showing which source each post uses), and images without alt text (body images with a missing or empty alt attribute plus featured images without alt, worst posts first, up to 20).
  • A bulk meta editor for fixing SEO titles, descriptions and focus keywords across many posts at once, and settings export/import as JSON — configuration only; keys and data never travel.
  • Webmaster verification for Google, Bing, Baidu, Yandex, Pinterest and Norton Safe Web (plus custom meta tags): paste the code or the full meta tag — the code is extracted automatically — and the tags are printed in the head while head output is active.
  • A Status & Tools page: a copyable system status report (plugin, WordPress, theme, plugins, server, database, constants, filesystem permissions) with a read-only error log viewer, plus database maintenance tools — clear the plugin cache/transients, clear the 404 log, re-create missing plugin tables, and recalculate all SEO scores in batches.

Switching is safe

The migration tool imports post meta and Open Graph data, redirects, and a subset of schema from your previous SEO plugin. It previews counts before it runs, never overwrites data SoraDigital SEO Optimizer already has, and never deletes the source data — so rolling back is simply reactivating the old plugin. If another SEO plugin is active, SoraDigital SEO Optimizer automatically disables its own head output to prevent duplicate tags.

External services

This plugin can connect to the external services below only when an administrator enables the relevant module and configures their own credentials in the plugin settings. Nothing is sent anywhere before that, and the plugin never contacts the author’s servers — there are none.

  • Google Indexing API (https://indexing.googleapis.com) — used by the Indexing API module to notify Google when URLs are published, updated or deleted. Data sent: the URL and the notification type (URL_UPDATED or URL_DELETED), sent when a post is published/updated/deleted or when an administrator runs the queue manually. Authentication uses OAuth2 with your own Google Cloud service account keys; the service account must be an owner of the site property in Google Search Console for Google to accept notifications. Terms of Service: https://developers.google.com/terms — Privacy Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy
  • Google Search Console API (https://searchconsole.googleapis.com) — used by the Search Console module with a read-only scope and your own service account keys. It retrieves clicks, impressions, CTR and average position statistics for the property you configure and displays them in wp-admin; no site content is sent. The module also calls the URL Inspection endpoint of the same API: when an administrator clicks a “Check index status” button (or the weekly keyword snapshot runs), the plugin sends the inspected post URL and the configured property identifier to Google and stores the returned index verdict in the post’s metadata. Terms of Service: https://developers.google.com/terms — Privacy Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy
  • IndexNow (https://api.indexnow.org) — used only when an administrator enables IndexNow in the plugin settings. When a post is published or its slug changes (or the administrator clicks the manual submit button), the plugin sends the site host, the site’s public IndexNow API key, the key file location and the list of affected public URLs to the IndexNow endpoint, which relays them to participating search engines. The API key is not a secret: it is published by the plugin itself at /{key}.txt on your own site, as the protocol requires. Protocol documentation: https://www.indexnow.org/documentation — Terms of Service and privacy information: https://www.indexnow.org/terms

Service account private keys are stored encrypted in your own WordPress database.

upgrade_notice.2.9.5: Admin UI restyle: tabbed pages now match the SoraDigital Internal Linker look (filled pill tabs, card panels, gradient header banner), and pagination uses pill buttons. No settings or data changes.
upgrade_notice.2.9.4: Content Health lists are now paginated (20 per page), and the active-tab accent is now the Sora logo blue. No settings or data changes.
upgrade_notice.2.9.3: Small fix: active tab label is now bright green instead of near-black dark green. No settings or data changes.
upgrade_notice.2.9.2: Admin UI polish: green active-tab accent, status cards in one row, paginated 404 log, and tabbed Content Health and Migration pages. No settings or data changes.
upgrade_notice.2.9.1: Small Settings-page fix: the main "Save Settings" button no longer shows on the IndexNow and Tools tabs, which have their own buttons. No settings or data changes.
upgrade_notice.2.9.0: The Settings page now uses vertical tabs instead of one long page. Presentation only: the same form, fields, and save behavior — no settings or data changes.
upgrade_notice.2.8.1: Cosmetic only: the plugin description on the Plugins screen is now one short sentence. No behavior, settings, or data changes.
upgrade_notice.2.8.0: The plugin has been renamed to SoraDigital SEO Optimizer (new slug and text domain soradigital-seo-optimizer). Settings and all stored data are unchanged, and exports from older versions still import. Security hardening from the wordpress.org review is included: custom JSON-LD is validated before storage, JSON-LD output cannot break out of its script tag, admin strings are escaped on output, and admin scripts are enqueued properly.
upgrade_notice.2.6.0: The text FAQ shortcode parser now handles every wpautop output form, so [sora_faq] text sections render exactly as their schema did. Posts without a HowTo shortcode/block may gain a detected HowTo schema node from a steps section (min. 3 steps). No settings or data are changed.
upgrade_notice.2.5.3: Code hygiene only — comments were cleaned up; the plugin behaves exactly as in 2.5.2. No settings or data are changed.
upgrade_notice.2.5.2: One fix: the version-upgrade routine (re-registering and soft-flushing rewrite rules on version change) now also triggers on front-end requests, not only in wp-admin, so file-overwrite updates get working routes without an admin visit. No settings or data are changed.
upgrade_notice.2.5.1: Fixes two silent issues: text-pattern FAQ shortcodes could render nothing on wpautop-processed content (schema unaffected), and file-overwrite updates never received newer rewrite rules. The upgrade routine now re-registers and soft-flushes the plugin's rewrite rules automatically.
upgrade_notice.2.5.0: Adds IndexNow notifications (off by default), global per-post-type schema templates, three new content health scans (duplicate titles, duplicate descriptions, images without alt text), a video sitemap and a Google News sitemap. No existing settings or data are changed.
upgrade_notice.2.4.0: Adds a hardcoded-TOC guard with language-aware TOC titles, settings export/import (configuration only), and a bulk meta editor. No settings or data are changed by the upgrade; posts that already contain a hardcoded TOC will simply stop receiving the automatic TOC.
upgrade_notice.2.3.0: Adds URL Inspection index status checks and weekly keyword position snapshots to the Search Console module. A new weekly WP-Cron event is scheduled automatically; index status results are cached in a new post meta key and snapshots in a new option. No settings change.
upgrade_notice.2.2.0: The interface is now in English with full translation support; the bundled Indonesian (id_ID) translation keeps the previous wording on Indonesian sites. No settings or data changes.
upgrade_notice.2.1.1: Public-package preparation only: migration keys are written as literals (same values as before) and the wordpress.org readme was added. No settings or data changes.
